---
title: "South Florida Insurance Market Analysis"
---

This project explores demographic and economic characteristics across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. These patterns can help describe communities, but they do not tell us whether any person or household will buy insurance.

## Income and age across block groups

```{r}
#| label: load-acs-data
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)

acs_data <- read_csv(
  "data/south-florida-block-groups.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    county = factor(
      county,
      levels = c("Miami-Dade", "Broward", "Palm Beach")
    )
  )
```

Each point represents one Census block group. The 2024 ACS five-year estimates show a weak overall relationship between median age and median household income (correlation: `r round(cor(acs_data$median_age, acs_data$median_household_income), 2)`). The county colors overlap, and there is wide variation within each county.

```{r}
#| label: income-age-scatterplot
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "Scatterplot of median household income and median age for South Florida Census block groups, colored by county."

ggplot(
  acs_data,
  aes(
    x = median_household_income,
    y = median_age,
    color = county
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Miami-Dade" = "#0072B2",
      "Broward" = "#E69F00",
      "Palm Beach" = "#009E73"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k", accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Income and age vary across South Florida",
    x = "Median household income (USD)",
    y = "Median age (years)",
    color = "County",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020–2024 ACS 5-year estimates."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

The graph uses **`r format(nrow(acs_data), big.mark = ",")` block groups**. The download retained rows with non-missing median income and median age; auxiliary housing and population estimates may still be missing. See the [ACS data source](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/data.html).
